svg.text: Soldering view — NEW pin map for BOTH halves · case upside down
Each COLOUR = one diode: starts at its switch's pin 2, crosses its own switch, band in the gap below,
then its leg runs along the gap and CROSSES the next key's leg = solder joint (grey dot). Colour changes = next diode.
Blue = wire where legs can't reach. Yellow = column wire on pin 1. DOTTED = cable from that end to its controller hole.
Controller drawn ABOVE the keys at its real left/right spot (it actually sits under the top keys), seen from its back, USB to the back edge. Shown 1.4x size.
Turquoise holes (right board) = trackball sensor wires: 006 MOTION, 008 SCLK, 011 SDIO, 104 NCS, VCC, GND.
Rewire controller ends and flash matching firmware. Keep the existing diode chains and key positions unchanged.
ROWS (blue) → controller holes, same holes on both boards
Esc Tab Cmd Lower Space Enter
COLUMNS (yellow) → controller holes, same holes on both boards
Trackball sensor → RIGHT board only (6 extra wires, turquoise holes)
tells the board the ball moved
ground: the GND next to RAW
017 edge = side with 017…024. 031 edge = side with RST/VCC. Read the printed label, not just the hole count.
C5 / 106 = LEFT Enter only (no right wire). First five columns consecutive; skip 011 / 104 for LEFT Enter (106). VDDIO / NRESET: unconnected.
LEFT HALF — case upside down (what you see while soldering)
RIGHT HALF — case upside down (what you see while soldering)
